touches.text: A device talks to other devices only over the bus, never by importing them.
The exceptions are client tools a device publishes:
Librarian: the embedding links work better without device boundaries in the way (4.5.2).

Ownership. The librarian owns every tree and delegates some to the devices that learn. EVERYTHING THAT LEARNS USING OUR GRAPH TREES IS A DELEGATE (CodeMother, chart and any learning block are examples, not a list), and each holds its trees by the librarian's delegation (Law 6: delegation through the owner's gate). WHY: two holders with different weights over the same nodes have different perspectives and can debate points, and the librarian, asked anything, can look at the query from both.

Cross-domain questions (cognition questions): inherently cross domain, not domain specific. "How might that work?" is Akien's number one: "it's applicable in almost all domains, and captures the pattern, not the domain specific answer." They are not design questions: a design question is a spec choice waiting on Akien (cairn question, CairnCommons/questions/).

The corpus is a git JSON file beside the librarian's code (shareable spec, 4.3.4); the question trees are derived from it. Every entry carries its origin: verbatim (Akien's words, with date and source) or proposed (by CC, by Gemini, ...). All questions are included; the origin keeps his words apart. "i expect i have a couple of hundred in my own head."
Any device reaching into the librarian's code other than through the trees tool it publishes. A delegate working its own trees through that tool is the delegation of 4.3.1.4, not a breach.
Walks go through the librarian's published trees tool, not the bus (2.3.7.1.2).

Most devices submit queries to the trees and never walk them: walk, nearest and neighbors are encapsulated by the librarian, which owns the processes of memory the way CodeMother owns the code. WHY: "that's why we have the librarian at all, to encapsulate and own those processes."
Owns the graph trees: the one list of nodes, and each depositor's index over them (4.3.1.1). Owns all learning in the system and delegates it (4.3.1.4); CC's learning records belong here too.
The trees tool's charter lists in its public interface what it offers: the module, and deposit_keyed, find and the keyed leaf's shape beside it. Akien 2026-11-09, answering Q#77.

Watcher face: watches the code and the builders' work over time, reasons over it with graph trees (held by the librarian's delegation), and learns the failure modes. Learns from: code, chat logs, books, past projects, CC's failure modes.
